# Drawer

Drawer that slides in from the right, for viewing details or editing longer content without leaving the
current page.

**Interaction**: when it opens, focus moves into the drawer and `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` cycle inside it; `Esc`
closes it, and focus returns to the element that was focused before opening.

**Category**: Feedback · **Common uses**: Details and editing that keep the context of a list, such as member details, permission settings or conversation settings

## Import

```ts
import { Drawer } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

### Basic usage

Slides in from the right to show details while keeping the context of the list.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Descriptions, Drawer, Section } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Basic() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>View member</Button>
      <Drawer title="Alex Morgan" open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} width={480}>
        <Section level={4} title="Details">
          <Descriptions
            column={1}
            items={[
              { key: 'team', label: 'Team', children: 'Design' },
              { key: 'role', label: 'Role', children: 'Editor' },
            ]}
          />
        </Section>
      </Drawer>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Footer actions

Put Cancel and Save in `footer`: they stay at the bottom while the content scrolls. Submit the form from the
footer with the instance from `Form.useForm()`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Drawer, Form, Inline, Input, Select } from 'vellum-ui'

export function WithFooter() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [form] = Form.useForm<{ name: string; role: string }>()
  const close = () => setOpen(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Edit member</Button>
      <Drawer
        title="Edit member"
        open={open}
        onClose={close}
        width={480}
        footer={
          <Inline justify="end">
            <Button onClick={close}>Cancel</Button>
            <Button variant="primary" onClick={() => form.submit()}>
              Save
            </Button>
          </Inline>
        }
      >
        <Form
          form={form}
          layout="vertical"
          initialValues={{ name: 'Alex Morgan', role: 'editor' }}
          onFinish={close}
        >
          <Form.Item label="Name" name="name" rules={[{ required: true, message: 'Enter a name' }]}>
            <Input />
          </Form.Item>
          <Form.Item label="Role" name="role">
            <Select
              options={[
                { value: 'viewer', label: 'Viewer' },
                { value: 'editor', label: 'Editor' },
                { value: 'admin', label: 'Admin' },
              ]}
            />
          </Form.Item>
        </Form>
      </Drawer>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the drawer is shown. Set it to false in `onClose`. Keep the Drawer rendered and switch `open`: a Drawer that is rendered only while it is open (`{show && <Drawer open />}`) disappears at once when it closes, without its closing animation. | — | No |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | Title in the header. | — | No |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Content of the drawer. It is unmounted after the drawer has closed (when the closing animation ends), so a form in it starts afresh the next time the drawer opens. State owned outside the drawer survives. | — | No |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | Actions at the bottom, such as Cancel and Save, laid out with Inline (`justify="end"`). The footer stays visible while the content scrolls. | — | No |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | Called when the user closes the drawer: the close button, `Esc` or a click outside the drawer. | — | No |
| `width` | `number \| string` | Width of the drawer: a number in pixels or a CSS length. | `378` | No |
| `testId` | `string` | Test hook, rendered as `data-testid` on the drawer. | — | No |

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
